verses.1: But Saulus, still filled with threats and violence towards the teacher of the Lord, went to see the high priest.
verses.2: He sent letters to Damascus to the leaders there, so that if anyone were to find those who were on their way, both men and women, he could bring them to Jerusalem.
verses.3: And during his journey, he came across Damascus. Suddenly, a light from the sky illuminated him.
verses.4: And when he fell to the ground, he heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?”
verses.5: He said, “Who are you, Lord?” He replied, “I am Jesus, whom you are seeking.”
verses.6: But rise up and go into the city. Then tell them what they must do for you.
verses.7: But the men who accompanied him stood still, listening to his voice, but not looking around.
verses.8: Saul rushed out of the land. With his eyes covered, he couldn’t see anything. They carried him into Damascus.
verses.9: And for three days, he did not see anything; he also did not eat or drink anything.
verses.10: There was also a student in Damascus named Anania. The Lord said to him out loud: “Anania.” He replied, “I am here, Lord.”
verses.11: And the Lord said to him: “Anastasius, go to the place called Eutheia. Seek out Judas Saulus, who is known as Tarses. For he is praying there.”
verses.12: And he saw a man in the sky, named Ananias. The man came up to him and put his hands on him, so that he could see clearly.
verses.13: Anania replied, “Lord, I have heard from many people about this man’s actions towards your saints in Jerusalem. What evil he has done to them!”
verses.14: And it also has the authority to appoint all those who are called by your name as priests.
verses.15: And the Lord said to him, “Go ahead, for this man is a vessel chosen by God to make my name known among the nations and kings of Israel.”
verses.16: For I will show him all that he must suffer for my name.
verses.17: Ananias went away and entered the house. When he arrived there, he put his hands on him and said, “Saul, my brother, the Lord has sent me to you. This Jesus will appear to you along your journey, so that you may receive the Holy Spirit.
verses.18: And immediately, they fell from his eyes like pieces of paper. He also looked away and then baptized himself.
verses.19: And by taking food, he strengthened himself. After that, some days passed among his students in Damascus.
verses.20: And immediately, in the crowd, Jesus announced that He was indeed the Son of God.
verses.21: And all those who heard this said, “Surely this is not the same person who called out those people in Jerusalem with that name. And surely he was sent here to bring them before the priests.”
verses.22: Saul, however, was even more determined to continue his efforts against the Jews who lived in Damascus. He believed that this man was indeed the Christ.
verses.23: But when days passed without any progress, the Jews decided to release him.
verses.24: But Saul knew about their plan. They also kept the gates open day and night, so that he could get inside.
verses.25: And when the disciples took him away at night, they lay down beside his bed, covering him with a blanket.
verses.26: When he arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to make a difference among the disciples. But everyone was afraid of him, as they didn’t believe that he was really a disciple at all.
verses.27: Barnabas, having taken him along, brought him before the apostles. He told them how he had seen the Lord on the way, and that the Lord had spoken to him. He also described how he met Jesus in Damascus under the name of Jesus.
verses.28: And while he was with them, he traveled and went to Jerusalem, rejoicing in the name of the Lord.
verses.29: He also tried to get along with the Hellenists. But they refused to let him do so.
verses.30: Knowing this, the brothers brought him to Caesarea and sent him to Tarsus.
verses.31: Thus, the church had peace throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria. It also spread as a result of the fear inspired by the Lord and the influence of the Holy Spirit.
verses.32: And it happened that Peter went through all those places, and also went to the holy people who lived in Lydda.
verses.33: There he found a man named Ainean, who had been trapped in a hole for eight years. He was completely exhausted.
verses.34: And Peter said to him, “Thank you, Lord Jesus Christ. Rise up and walk among us.” And he immediately stood up.
verses.35: And all those who lived in Lydda and Sira, they saw him as well. They returned to their masters.
verses.36: In Ioppi, there was a teacher named Tavitha. She was also known as Dorcas. She was someone who always did good deeds and was very kind-hearted.
verses.37: During those days, she became weaker and weaker until she died. They then placed her in a coffin.
verses.38: But when the disciples heard that Peter was among them, they sent two men to ask her not to go out until they arrived.
verses.39: But when Peter got up, he joined them. As soon as he arrived, they brought him to the upper room. All the women wept before him, and they showed him all the clothes and garments that Dorcas had made for them.
verses.40: When Peter pulled everyone out, he also pressed his knees together in prayer. Then, turning back to his body, he said, “Tabitha, stand up.” She opened her eyes and saw that Peter was there with her.
verses.41: He also raised her up with his hand, and by calling upon the saints, he made her live again.
verses.42: It became known throughout all of Ioppi, and many believed in Him.
verses.43: And a day came when it was time to leave Ioppe, in the presence of some Simon.
